testCases.input: What is covered under endorsement IMT 22A in two-wheeler policy?

testCases.name: test_case_3
testCases.input: How much will I get if my two-wheeler bike's tyre is damaged, and does it matter whether I have the Tyre and Rim add-on?
testCases.expectedOutput: Under the base policy (Section I, Clause 2b), damage to tyres and tubes is only payable if the vehicle is damaged at the same time, and even then, liability is limited to 50% of the replacement cost. If the TA34 Tyre and Rim Secure add-on is opted, standalone tyre damage (not requiring simultaneous vehicle damage) is covered, with payout based on unused tread depth: <3mm not covered, 3-5mm = 50%, 5-7mm = 75%, ≥7mm = 100% of the cost of a new tyre/tube, up to a maximum of 2 replacements per policy period.

testCases.name: test_case_6
testCases.input: Is water damage to my electric two-wheeler's engine and battery covered, and what add-ons would I need?
testCases.expectedOutput: Standard engine water-ingress damage is covered under Add-on TA33 (Engine Secure), but this cover explicitly does NOT apply to electric vehicles. For electric vehicles, water-related battery/charging equipment damage (including ingress of water while charging) is instead covered under Add-on TA27 (Electric Surge Secure), which covers arcing, self-heating, leakage of electricity, or short-circuiting including water ingress while charging, up to the vehicle's IDV. Depreciation on a replaced battery can further be recovered under TA28 (Depreciation Allowance - Battery), provided the battery cost is included in the IDV.

testCases.input: At what threshold is my car vehicle declared a Constructive Total Loss, and if that happens, does the base policy or the Return to Invoice add-on pay more?
testCases.expectedOutput: The vehicle is treated as a Constructive Total Loss if the aggregate cost of retrieval and/or repair exceeds 75% of the IDV. Under the base policy (Condition 3.III(a)), the Company's liability for Total Loss/CTL/Cash Loss is capped at the IDV of the vehicle (including accessories) as specified in the schedule, less the value of the wreck if opted by the customer. If the Return to Invoice add-on is opted, the Company additionally pays the Sum Insured under the add-on, calculated as the difference between the IDV and the total actual expenses incurred to acquire a new vehicle of similar make/model per the manufacturer's/dealer's on-road price — so Return to Invoice pays more than the base IDV-only settlement whenever the on-road price of a replacement exceeds the IDV.
